scope: Portfolio monitoring, REA references, graph tooling and GitHub source hosting
method: Official product/documentation pages reviewed for available capabilities. REA is assessed as an out-of-band analysis tool; no REA CLI/MCP run was available in this review. No wallets were connected and no code was modified by these services.

provenance: Official Step Finance announcement “Step Group Changes”, published 2025-11-04, says its dashboard, APIs, and mobile app would be sunset; accessed 2026-10-15.
The manifest homepage returned HTTP 404 in the unauthenticated 2026-10-15 URL probe.
discoveries: The vendor announced the Step dashboard, APIs, and mobile app wind-down; this is not a current integration target.
The listed homepage returned HTTP 404, consistent with the previously announced product wind-down.
No active Step Finance portfolio API contract was verified.
patterns: mark sunset vendor products unavailable to new runtime integrations
preserve historical provider references but reconcile accounting to confirmed chain state
sources.overlap: Historical portfolio dashboard/API source only; no current runtime integration is justified.
risks: Vendor announced product sunset; URLs or APIs may disappear or be repurposed.
Historical indexed balances are not realized PnL and must not become execution or risk authority.
validation: Do not configure this domain as a live API or wallet-review dependency.
For historical records, compare sampled positions against canonical RPC and confirmed execution records.
sources.license: Hosted service; product sunset; historical reuse terms not established

provenance: Official SonarWatch migration website says SonarWatch is joining the Jupiter team to build a portfolio tracker and identifies the SONAR token migration; accessed 2026-10-15.
The manifest sonar.watch hostname failed DNS resolution during the unauthenticated 2026-10-15 URL probe.
discoveries: SonarWatch announced it was joining the Jupiter team to build a portfolio tracker; the product lineage now points to Jupiter Portfolio.
The original hostname did not resolve during the current availability check, while the official migration page remains available.
No current portfolio API contract or trading-authority role was verified.
patterns: resolve product ownership and migration before relying on a legacy domain
keep portfolio views advisory and reconcile values to raw account state and confirmed signatures
sources.overlap: Secondary portfolio visibility only; no engine integration or execution authority established. The product lineage points to Jupiter Portfolio.
risks: Legacy domain resolution and ownership changed; old endpoints risk silent service loss.
Protocol coverage and indexed valuations may lag; portfolio estimates are not realized PnL.
validation: Use the official migration and successor-product documentation to select any replacement endpoint.
Compare sampled holdings and transactions against canonical RPC and confirmed execution records before labeling them reconciled.
sources.license: Hosted service; successor-product terms require review

provenance: Official Helius Orb product page entry; exact current functionality requires direct docs review.
discoveries: Listed as Helius portfolio/wallet data product for Solana.
Product outputs should be treated as indexed views until verified against chain state.
patterns: Use wallet monitoring to identify reconciliation candidates, not as sole balance authority.
Log provider freshness and asset coverage.
overlap: Potential Helius data surface overlaps portfolio dashboards, not execution authority.
risks: Wallet address privacy and API plan constraints.
validation: Review current docs and data freshness details.
Compare representative accounts against RPC/token-account state.

discoveries: graph-tool is a Python library for efficient graph analysis and visualization.
Algorithms operate on a graph supplied by the analyst; they do not establish wallet attribution.
patterns: Prototype large graph algorithms over timestamped, provenance-bearing wallet edges.
Keep visualization/centrality results separate from direct evidence.
overlap: Offline analytics only; no runtime integration.
risks: Installation/platform constraints and algorithm assumptions need review.
validation: Use synthetic graphs with known relationships.
Reproduce results with a simpler reference algorithm on small samples.

provenance: REA project website; repository docs previously reviewed in batch 005.
discoveries: REA is positioned as a reverse-engineering/analysis toolkit with task-specific workflows.
The website is product context; capability and permission claims should be grounded in versioned docs.
patterns: Use REA out of band to map code/artifact structure and formulate test hypotheses.
Keep tool findings separate from runtime facts and authorization decisions.
overlap: Independent verification tooling; not part of feed, risk or execution pipelines.
risks: Static structural mapping cannot prove runtime execution or semantic equivalence.
Tool version and capability mismatch can invalidate assumptions.
validation: Pin REA version and record exact command, target and outputs.
Confirm any hypothesized behavior with deterministic SYLPH tests.

provenance: REA guides index; individual guide references reviewed in batch 005 where available.
discoveries: Guides provide workflow-specific instructions for REA operations.
Each workflow has its own supported inputs, boundaries and evidence strength.
patterns: Choose a workflow based on target type and explicit authorization.
Preserve command/config/version and output for reproducibility.
overlap: Supports analysis process, not SYLPH runtime.
risks: Guide examples may drift from installed package behavior.
Do not generalize static analysis claims to runtime behavior.
validation: Match guide revision to pinned REA package version.
Use source tests/runtime identity evidence for claims about execution.

discoveries: Showcases demonstrate examples of tool output and workflows.
Showcase results are examples, not proof of coverage for SYLPH or other targets.
patterns: Use examples to understand output shape, then validate behavior on the actual target.
Record unsupported or unverified mappings explicitly.
risks: Demo results can be mistaken for guarantees.
Showcases may use different versions or environments.
validation: Reproduce on a pinned local package and representative fixture.
Keep conclusions bounded to observed artifacts.

provenance: npm package listing; prior REA package docs/context reviewed in batch 005.
discoveries: Package registry is a distribution/version source for REA Agents.
Package listing/version alone does not establish installed binary identity or capabilities.
patterns: Pin exact package version and integrity hash.
Record package source, lockfile and invocation with audit evidence.
validation: Verify package integrity, release provenance and current security policy.
Run only in isolated analysis environment with least privilege.
sources.license: See package metadata at pinned version

provenance: GitHub platform reference; repository-specific material is covered by individual source records.
discoveries: GitHub hosts source, release history, issues and pull-request evidence.
A URL or repository claim alone does not prove code quality, maintenance or safety.
patterns: Pin commit/release digests and review actual source files.
Record upstream license, activity and provenance before adopting code.
overlap: Hosting platform, not an integration component.
risks: Mutable branches, compromised accounts/releases and misleading metadata.
Repository presence does not imply permission to copy or deploy.
validation: Verify commit signatures/provenance where available and inspect license.
Use reproducible builds and dependency scanning before adoption.
